To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we developed a service-oriented P 2 P system that supports the creation of context-aware communities, and (b) the AXML language provides a simple, yet powerful, query language for the superdatabase of P 2 P systems.

(a) the DBGlobe infrastructure is a peer-to-peer superdatabase that is capable of supporting the creation and maintenance of context-dependent communities; (b) the DBGlobe metadata management system provides a flexible and efficient way to model and query data that are encapsulated in autonomous services; and (c) the AXML query language allows users to formulate queries on services and data in a simple and natural way.

(1) the service-oriented approach to P2P data management is feasible; (2) a query language that combines path queries with service calls is useful; (3) the use of location-dependent metadata is essential for the creation of communities; (4) the use of mobile peers is feasible; (5) a hierarchical routing mechanism is useful for path queries; and (6) the use of context-dependent communities is feasible
